full.description: This is a low-power photomicrograph of an oral mucosal lesion stained with hematoxylin and eosin. The section shows a well-circumscribed submucosal lesion consisting of numerous proliferating capillaries and a mixed inflammatory infiltrate within a loose fibrous stroma. The overlying stratified squamous epithelium is thin and attenuated at the apex. These histopathologic features are characteristic of a pyogenic granuloma (lobular capillary hemangioma) of the oral mucosa.

These clinical features are characteristic of a mucous retention phenomenon. The most likely diagnosis is a mucocele of the oral cavity.

random.description: This is a low-power photomicrograph of a skin or mucosal biopsy stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E). The section shows a well-circumscribed, highly vascular proliferation in the superficial dermis or submucosa, surrounded by a thin epidermal or mucosal collar (often referred to as an epidermal collarette). The lesion is composed of numerous small, proliferating capillaries lined by plump endothelial cells, accompanied by a mixed inflammatory infiltrate. These histological features are characteristic of a pyogenic granuloma (lobular capillary hemangioma).
